decision.statement: Which off-the-shelf chat interface should we use for this project's launch?
decision.description: Scope: single VPS, self-hosted, Tailscale-only access, multi-provider chat, privacy control, history import/analysis, low ops burden, and strong mobile browser rendering. This matrix is qualitative (no weighted scoring).

options.label: Open WebUI
options.description: Current baseline; Docker + SQLite; fastest operational path.

options.label: AnythingLLM
options.description: RAG-centric platform; less chat-first for this phase.

Open WebUI.text: Ready now with minimal integration risk

LibreChat.text: Strong option, but more setup than current baseline

AnythingLLM.text: Deployable, but less aligned to chat-first launch

Build simple custom UI.text: Not launch-ready without significant build effort
No import until migration tooling is built

Open WebUI.text: Local SQLite and exports are analysis-friendly

AnythingLLM.text: Usable but less focused on chat-history analytics

LobeChat.text: Possible with more infra and query work

Build simple custom UI.text: Fully controllable schema and analytics pipelines

Open WebUI.text: Works, but endpoint or model routing may need tuning

AnythingLLM.text: Less ideal for this specific chat/API requirement

LobeChat.text: Moderate compatibility with higher ops cost

Build simple custom UI.text: Direct control over endpoint selection and adapters

Open WebUI.text: Strong local-first posture with configurable telemetry

AnythingLLM.text: Acceptable, but needs careful configuration review

Open WebUI.text: Lowest ops overhead in current stack

LobeChat.text: High ops burden among off-the-shelf choices

Open WebUI.text: Good portability with a reasonable extension path

AnythingLLM.text: Moderate portability for this use case

Build simple custom UI.text: Full control and portability of architecture

Open WebUI.text: Generally good responsive behavior in mobile browsers

LibreChat.text: Good mobile web experience; verify provider-specific views

AnythingLLM.text: Usable on mobile web, but UX focus is less chat-centric

LobeChat.text: Strong UI potential on mobile, pending heavier deploy setup

Build simple custom UI.text: Can be excellent on mobile, but only after dedicated UI work
